name: Temple Street
desc: South of Mong Kok is a great place to eat Chinese street food. You have not been to Honkers unless you have eaten in this street. Temple Street, famously featured in Chinese cinema, is one of the few pedestrianised stree

name: Chungking Mansions
desc: Houses many budget Indian, Nepali and African restaurants. Touts at the front entrance will lead you to the restaurants via the small rickety lifts. Be warned that the competition between the touts can become very open,

name: CitySuper
addr: 3/F, Gateway Arcade, Harbour City, Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
desc: A local upscale supermarket chain with pan Asian, Western style food and has its own food court in Harbour City on Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui.

name: Choi Lung Restaurant
desc: A typical local Chinese restaurant offering dim sum and a Cantonese style dinner. Dim Sum starts from $4.80. It is a nightclub after seven with contemporary music.

name: Dragon Centre Food Court
addr: 8/F, Dragon Centre, 37K Yen Chow Street, Sham Shui Po
desc: This food court provides a variety of Chinese, Southeast Asian and Western cuisines at attractive prices. Dishes range from $10 up.

name: Fa Yuen Street Complex
desc: A complex consisting of a wet market, cooked food centre, sports centre and a public library. It is a place where you can find cheap and genuine Hong Kong style food in Kowloon. There was only one small food stall open o

name: Mr. Wong's
desc: This one is popular with exchange students in Hong Kong, offering all the food you can eat and all the beer you can drink .

name: Swagat
desc: On the first floor of Chungking Mansions, this is arguably one of the best Indian restaurants in Hong Kong.

name: Tim Ho Wan
desc: It is said to be the cheapest Michelin starred restaurant in the world, serving a variety of dim sum dishes starting at $10. Be prepared to wait one, two or even three hours if you come on a busy day (you get a numbered

name: Jade Palace
addr: 4/F, Star House, Canton Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
desc: A tasty and tourist-friendly dim sum spot. Order by selecting from a card (also in English), not from a cart. Try the shrimp and chive dumplings and the tripe in ginger soup. Dim sum served 11AM-3PM daily, dishes $16-40

name: Red Ant
addr: G/F, 27 Ashley Rd, Tsim Sha Tsui
desc: A modern bistro-like restaurant with a wide selection of light meals and snacks. No alcohol is served but there is a long list of fresh juices and teas.

name: Yat Tung Heen
addr: Eaton Hotel, 380 Nathan Road, Kwun Chung
desc: Cantonese dishes and dim sum, from traditional favourites to original creations.

name: Aberdeen Seafood Restaurant
price: Eat outside on the pavement and watch th

name: Green
desc: Contemporary cafe and restaurant located within the modern Hotel Icon. Lunch offers set menus with lobster, pasta and more. Nice desserts and wine list. The interior is beautiful, with one of the world's largest indoor v

name: La Taverna Restaurant
desc: Hong Kong's oldest Italian restaurant sits hidden in plain view at the end of busy Ashley Road. Stepping through the door is like stepping back in time to a Hong Kong of the past or at least an Italian version of it circ

name: Oi Man Sang
addr: Sham Shui Po Building, 1A-1C Shek Kip Mei St
desc: This outdoor kitchen may be the last outdoor food stall still cooking over the extreme heat of kerosene, wok hei-style. Expect to stand in line for a bit.

name: Fook Lam Moon
desc: The yum cha/dim sum is excellent. The service and decor is also impressive. Expect to pay around $55 per serve for the mid range dishes. The English menu is only a small subset of the Chinese menu so take along someone w

name: Gaddi's
addr: Peninsula Hotel, Salisbury Road, Tsim Sha Tsui
desc: Arguably Hong Kong's leading restaurant that has delighted aficionados of French food and wine for over 80 years. This is the place where you can test your own command of the French language against French-speaking Chine

name: Morton's The Steakhouse
desc: The Hong Kong location for this famous chain of American steakhouses, Morton's has one best in the city multiple times. With views overlooking the harbour, great service and classic cocktails - combined with thick steaks

name: Nobu
desc: The HK location for this exclusive Japanese restaurant. Nobu has delicate bento box lunches and decadent dinners and desserts. Remarkable service and drinks, and a view overlooking the Harbour that is worth the price. Dr

name: Aqua
desc: Nearby at the top of the 1 Peking Road office building is an alternative and less touristy spot with equally impressive views. As well as a bar, they have a Japanese and Italian restaurant for those without a budget.

name: Biergarten
desc: This friendly German bar is one of the few places in Kowloon where you can find a good range of quality beers. Excellent German food is served — not just sausages and sauerkraut. Use Exit N2 at East Tsim Sha Tsui MTR sta

name: Felix
desc: Atop the Peninsula Hotel on Salisbury Rd, is known for its Philippe Starck interior and the views of the harbour skyline, whilst the men's bathroom has an impressive view up Nathan Road. According to legend, the world's

name: Hutong
desc: Hutong is a great place to get a good view of Hong Kong from the top floor of a business building. It's a Michelin starred restaurant with amazing food — try the signature crispy lamb breast with garlic and ginger.

name: Knutsford Terrace
desc: Near the Miramar hotel is perhaps best described as the 'Lang Kwai Fong' of Kowloon, and has a large number of bars and restaurants of variable quality that cater for mid-range budgets. A little smaller and less phreneti

name: Ashley Road
desc: Between Nathan Road and the Ocean Terminal shopping mall, features many Western restaurants and bars.

name: Mody Road/Centennial Garden
desc: Close to many good hotels, this area of Tsim Sha Tsui offers a more relaxed environment for a drink. Here you will find bars and restaurants spilling out onto the pavement. Leave East Tsim Sha Tsui station at Exit P1, an

name: Tung Choi Street
desc: Between Prince Edward Road and Boundary Street, is one of Kowloon's up-and-coming bar strips. Few tourists or expats venture here, but there are nearly two dozen bars. Some specialize in karaoke while others have open fr

name: Dumpling House
desc: Great Beijing-style dumplings, avoid going there during lunch hour, because it is packed.

name: Good Luck Thai
desc: Seating is both indoors and outdoors, very popular on weekends, nice atmosphere.

name: Law Fu Kee
desc: Popular little restaurant serving congee and noodles.

name: Wai Kee Congee Shop
desc: A good place to sample some traditional Hong Kong style food.

name: XTC Gelato
desc: A popular place to get your fix of ice cream or frozen yoghurt.

name: Zhong Guo Song
addr: Wo On Lane, Lan Kwai Fong
desc: Good Chinese food, without MSG and less oil.

name: L16 Cafe and Bar
addr: Hong Kong Park, 19 Cotton Tree Drive
desc: Serves Thai and Italian food, but come for the location - not the food. A rare place to drink and eat outside away from the noise of Central.

name: Maxim's Palace
desc: One of Hong Kong's most popular dim sum spots, featuring harbour views if you're lucky enough to score a window table. The atmosphere and food are very much in the classical dim sum tradition, a large, noisy hall with wa

name: Pizza Express
desc: Has a nice view overlooking the Mid-Levels Escalator.

name: Yung Kee Restaurant
desc: This is a popular place for Cantonese-style roast goose and century eggs. Come early and make reservations as they have been known to run out of geese!

name: Baci
desc: Pizza.

name: Beirut
desc: Lebanese cuisine is top of the sheet. Lamb or chicken kebab and sisha. Nice decor but the food is a far cry from the real deal (particularly in taste).

name: Tokyo Joe
desc: Japanese food.

name: Fung Shing Restaurant
desc: Very local eatery known for its dim sum, which is cheap and good at $10 and up per serving. Open daily from 7:30AM for the dim sum breakfast crowd, but no English menu.

name: Al Dente
addr: 16 Staunton St, Soho (中環蘇豪士丹頓街16號地下)
desc: Italian cuisine. Serving large, medium quality dishes not too different from what you would find in an Italian bistro. Their pastas and meat dishes are better than their pizzas. Often full.

name: Ayuthaiya
addr: 35 Hollywood Rd, Soho (中環荷李活道35號)
desc: Thai cuisine. Serving quite authentic food in a stylish, dark environment.

name: Brunch Club
desc: Neighbourhood-style Western coffee shop (pre-Starbucks style) specialising in brunch and breakfast, although dinner is also served. Customers are provided with a wide range of newspapers and magazines in English and Chin

name: Double Happiness Cafe
desc: Shanghai cuisine. Nice and simple little restaurant serving authentic Shanghainese dishes. Prices reflects that this is in the centre of Soho and comparable food can be found much cheaper elsewhere.

name: Jashan
desc: Indian cuisine. Serves great curries and perfect naan. The lunch buffet is good value.

name: Oola
addr: G/F, Centre Stage, Bridges St, Soho
desc: Away from the crowds in Soho, but worth the extra walk. International menu in a comfortable environment. Serves as both a place to eat or drink. Drinks are expensive.

name: La Pampa
desc: Argentinian.

name: The Peak Lookout
desc: Serving a range of international cuisine such as naan bread, Hainan chicken, and steaks in a 19th-century heritage building. Also has a pleasant garden patio.

name: Percy Bakery
addr: Shop b, g/f, 68 Catchick St, Kennedy Town
desc: A high quality bakery. Take away and delivery service only.

name: 8½ Otto e Mezzo Bombana
desc: Only Italian restaurant outside Italy to be awarded three Michelin stars.

name: Bistro Bouchon
desc: French bistro focusing on steaks.

name: Chez Patrick
desc: An excellent, Parisian-style French restaurant. The proprietor, Patrick, has a delightful obsession with foie gras which extends to creative dishes such as foie gras ice cream served as a first course.

name: Chilli Fagara
desc: Sichuan cuisine. Great spicy dishes including the favourites you will find in Sichuan Province. This restaurant's ambitions appear to go further than just making the food as the mainland original implying that some might

name: Luk Yu Tea House
desc: Famous for the excellent tea and traditional dim sum. It is a popular meeting place for businessmen. They provide an English menu on request.

name: HAHAClub
desc: For cheaper booze, you can try here.

name: Works
desc: A good place for tourists to start on the gay bar-scene. Popular with expats and tourists alike, it is easily accessible in Central. Friday and Saturday are the most popular nights but do not expect many drinkers to arri

name: 65 Peel
desc: A bar with a very Hong Kong aesthetic serving cocktails and a range of locally brewed beer.

name: de België
desc: A bar specialising in Belgian beers.

name: Craft Brew & Co
desc: A corner bar with a selection of craft beer on tap.

name: The Globe
desc: Excellent beer pub, also has good menu aimed at western taste buds. It is also one of the few places that has Typhoon T8 on tap, a locally produced cask ale.

name: Staunton's Wine Bar & Cafe
desc: A western-style restaurant with a bar on the ground floor and table service upstairs.

name: Propaganda
desc: Famous gay club. Tends to get going after Works has faded.

name: Chiu Yuen
desc: Small and usually packed eatery serving up a wide range of simple fare, but the crowd-pullers are the beef brisket noodles (a scarcely believable $13) and the homemade giant fishball soup ($16). Other branches are in Abe

name: Tsui Wah Restaurant
desc: Clean and multilingual, this is a moderately priced cha chaan teng where even a non-Chinese speaker can easily explore. Aside from the typical cha chaan teng foods such as French toast, curry, baked rice, fried noodles,

name: Cafe Kenon
addr: Shop 208, 2/F Tai Yau Plaza, 181 Johnston Rd, Wanchai
desc: Where affordable Italian food meets Chinese expectations.

name: Tai Hing Roast Restaurant
addr: G/F, Shop J, Po Ming Bldg, 49-57 Lee Garden Rd, Causeway Bay.
desc: A Cantonese BBQ eatery. Roast pork, roast piglet, BBQ pork, roast goose, soy sauce chicken are all hanging in the front display window, available to eat in or take out.

name: Loving Hut
addr: Shops B&C, G/F, The Hennessy, 256 Hennessy Rd
desc: Serving vegetarian and vegan fast food at affordable prices.

name: New Bangkok Restaurant
desc: Friendly staff serving excellent Thai food.

name: Hokkaido Dairy Farm
addr: Shop A-B, G/F, 211 Johnston Road, Wan Chai
desc: Ham, eggs, toast and Japanese milk. Very good for a light breakfast or lunch.

name: 3.6.9. Restaurant Shanghai
desc: Great old style dive usually packed with locals especially at lunch. Shanghai style Chinese food, excellent and inexpensive Xaio Long Bao. About as authentic as you'll find in this part of the island.

name: Baby Blue Cafe and Bar
addr: 3/F, Chuang's Enterprises Building, 382 Lockhart Road, Causeway Bay
desc: Western food served to meet Hong Kong taste buds.

name: The Quarterdeck Club
desc: Fenwick Pier, Wanchai. This is one of the few harbourside restaurants. Slightly spoiled by the land reclamation nearby

name: The Flying Pan
desc: On the corner of Lockhart Road and Luard Road. Look above Mes Amis and you will find the best place for breakfast and it's open all-day, everyday. This is the place where you can have a full-English washed down with a gl

name: Kung Tak Lam
desc: A delightful vegetarian restaurant serving Shanghainese cuisine. Hotpot, dim sum and noodles dishes are made with MSG free ingredients.

name: Chun Kee Restaurant
addr: 117-119 Shau Kei Wan Road, Sai Wan Ho
desc: Serves typical Chinese food from dumplings to Peking Duck.

name: Red Pepper Restaurant
desc: Causeway Bay (MTR: Causeway Bay). Sichuan cuisine; spicy dishes.

name: Pho Saigon
desc: 319, Hennessy Road, Wanchai, Hong Kong. Extremely good Vietnamese restaurant serving traditional dishes including Pho and Vietnamese coffee. Expect to pay around $120.

name: Tai Ping Koon Restaurant
desc: (太平館餐廳), 6 Pak Sha Road, Causeway Bay. Founded in Guangzhou in 1860, the three locations (two in Kowloon) have now become institutions of Canto-Western cuisine. Don't be put off by the touristy menu available in three la

name: Café One
desc: Causeway Bay, Open 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Fun & friendly informal dining from an open kitchen and an exciting buffet featuring a wide selection of Asian and Western cuisines.

name: Tony Roma's
desc: International food. This branch has the advantage of an outdoor terrace that enables you to eat and drink above the noise of the streets below.

name: Under the Bridge Spicy Crab
addr: Shop 1-2, G/F, 414 - 424 Jaffe Road, Causeway Bay
desc: This has become a Hong Kong institution that is famous for its Typhoon Shelter style crab. People come for the food not the interior which is basic.

name: West Villa Restaurant
desc: Its signature dim sum is the cha xiu bao (叉燒包) or roast pork buns that is served steamed, fried or as rolls. One of the items is named "Big Brother Chaxiu" after Hong Kong's film star Jacky Chan (Big Brother) who is fond

name: Fook Lam Moon
desc: The main branch of an old school Cantonese restaurant group with locations in Kowloon, Shanghai and Japan. Famous for luxurious delicacies such as abalone, and swallow's nest. More affordable specialties include roast su

name: The Coffee Academics
addr: G/F, Bigfoot Centre, 38 Yiu Wa St
desc: Great coffee a short walk from Times Square in Causeway bay. Coffee is roasted on premise and they have an outside sitting area.

name: The Cafe Corridor
desc: Small coffee shop directly opposite Time Square. Entrance is really small so look carefully. Good coffee for $26.

name: Café "1974"
addr: G/F, ICAC Building, 303 Java Road, North Point
desc: A coffee shop operated by Po Leung Kuk that also functions as the ICAC's museum. The shop was named after the year of establishment of the Independent Commission Against Corruption, and coffee is known to be one of the d

name: The Pawn
desc: Wan Chai. A Western-style bar and cafe in an attractive building that was once a pawn shop. It is away from the naughty parts of Wan Chai in one of the few historic buildings remaining in Hong Kong. It will appeal to vis

name: Joe Bananas
desc: This is one Hong Kong's most famous and popular bars, and can be highly recommended to younger travellers. Drinks are competitively priced, and staff are helpful and friendly.

name: Devils Advocate
desc: Popular with the rugby crowd with English pub food.

name: Kangaroo Pub
desc: Australian sports bar. Has a book exchange.

name: Carnegie's
desc: Rock music themed bar. Live bands playing occasionally, sports on multiple screens and a big screen, dancing the night away on the bar top.

name: The Canny Man
desc: Scottish style Whiskey Bar with a free pool table.

name: Skitz Sports Bar
desc: 5/F. Sports bar with pool tables, darts and big screens.

name: The Wanch
desc: A good bar for music lovers with live music playing every night. There is also a showcase of local bands held over several days around the 1st of July every year.

name: The Chapel
desc: Serves curry.

name: The Jockey
desc: A relaxed British style pub that serves food. When the weather suits this is a great place to sit outside and watch the world pass by.

name: Inn Side Out
desc: Also 'East End Brewing Company'.

name: Moon Garden Tea House
desc: A calming location in a busy part of town where you can choose from over 70 types of tea and, for a price, enjoy the Chinese ritual of tea served in tiny cups. Food is also served.

name: Dickens Bar
desc: Popular British-style sports bar in the basement of the Excelsior hotel. A good range of drinks and serves very good English food, including a notable curry lunch buffet.

name: Wo Sang
desc: Next to Kei Lun Light rail station in Tuen Mun. It is famous for its traditional Hong Kong dishes. You can sit next to the kitchen and watch how they cook the fried dishes. The roast goose here is also famous.

name: Learn Hop
desc: Next to the Siu Hong MTR station. Located inside the Siu Hong Commercial Complex. It is famous for its choice of Guangdong, wonton and dumpling noodles. Also serves Zha jiang mian.

name: Tai Po Hui Market
desc: A modern complex of small stalls. The must-try items are fried pork chop noodles and fish ball noodles. Also, for as little as $10 a dish, you can choose from a variety of culinary styles, including local favourites and

name: Chan Kun Kee
desc: Wo Che Estate, Sha Tin. A typical Dai Pai Dong in Hong Kong providing a variety of Cantonese dishes. Get off at Sha Tin Railway Station and take a taxi to Wo Che Estate.

name: Ho To Tai dumpling wonton noodle
addr: G/F, no.67, On Ning Road, Yuen Long

name: Fu Ah Seafood Restaurant
addr: G/F 27, Hoi Pong St, Sai Kung
desc: The second-to-last in Sai Kung's seafood restaurant alley, this unassuming joint does good set meals for $150/person, with reasonably priced beer and no surprises in the bill.

name: Dragon Inn Seafood Restaurant
addr: 19.5 Miles, Castle Peak Road, Tuen Mun
desc: is a famous seafood restaurant in Tuen Mun. The price is more valuable than Sai Kung and you can go to the Sam Shing market to choose your seafood which would provide more variation. It is ranked one of the best seafood

name: Shanghai Po Po
addr: Shop 3207, Phase 1, Tuen Mun Town Plaza, 3 Tuen Lung Street, Tuen Mun
desc: One of the best chain restaurant to eat the Shanghainese food. It serves big dishes at a value price. It's famous for its dan dan noodles and hot and sour soup.

name: Lung Wah Hotel
desc: It is famous for roasted pigeons.

name: Chinese and Thailand Seafood Restaurant
desc: Food here is reasonable and it offers probably the best meal in the village.

name: Spices Restaurant
addr: G/F The Arcade, 109 Repulse Bay Road, Repulse Bay
desc: Serves pan-Asian food with style. Excellent location, only a few minutes walk from the beach. You can choose to dine outside on the patio and enjoy superb views over Repulse Bay.

name: The Verandah
desc: Posh colonial-style Western dinning recreated in a modern building overlooking Repulse Bay.

name: The Boathouse
desc: A reasonably inexpensive restaurant on the Stanley promenade that features dining upstairs and a more relaxed bar on the ground floor.

name: The Smugglers Inn
desc: Located on the sea front, this is a British-style pub that serves a range of beers and traditional English pub food. It is along the Stanley promenade, and offers a great view of the ocean while relaxing with a drink.

name: Come Be Rich Restaurant
desc: A popular local banquet restaurant close to the ferry pier. This establishment has outdoor seating and is popular with families and large groups. The conversations here can get quite loud towards closing time.

name: Fooderful
desc: A larger restaurant with entrances at both ends and outdoor seating out the back facing towards the ferry pier. Most of the dishes are larger and intended to be shared, so this is more suitable for those coming in groups

name: Hoi King Seafood Restaurant
desc: A local seafood restaurant that also does traditional Hong Kong-style Yumcha dishes.

name: Kee Sum Cafe
addr: Shop B, G/F, 3 Peng Chau Wing On Street
desc: A very popular restaurant at the end of Wing On Street which is a very popular breakfast spot with locals.

name: Peng Chau Si Do
desc: A shop selling cold drinks and local Hong Kong snacks situated within the main ferry pier.

name: Wah Kee Snacks
desc: A local-style snack shop up one of the smaller alleys off the main shopping street.

name: Tino Club Thai Food
desc: A Thai restaurant on the Nam Wan Road with outdoor and indoor seating.

name: Viet Restaurant
desc: A Vietnamese restaurant on the main shopping street less than 5 minutes walk from the ferry pier.

name: Paris Cafe
desc: A newer establishment that sells local takes on more Westernised food.

name: The Old China Hand
desc: This is the one and only pub on Peng Chau. It serves draft beers and caters for the needs of most drinkers. Staff speak English, Cantonese, Japanese and Mandarin.

name: SunSatStore
desc: A small cafe / store selling a variety of antiques, crafts, and other objects that the owners have collected through their travels around the world.
